Revised working conclusion: the first audit was sound for the executable HTML/application layer, but it undercounted README/data-pack-only project families. The expanded inventory supports 206 content-scored HTML innovation candidates + 52 provisional documentation-only candidates = 258 in the expanded working set. The two layers are intentionally kept separate because the 52 supplemental records have not been scored to the same content depth as the 761 HTML families. This is not 258 patents, worldwide firsts, or validated inventions.

tier distribution

A ≥62 = strong internal audit candidate; B 58–61.9 = credible candidate; C 52–57.9 = exploratory; D <52 = preserve but do not count toward the headline estimate.

what the strict shortlist means

27 project families met a tougher heuristic: experimental/field-test status, maturity ≥55, evidence signal ≥30, and a distinctiveness proxy ≥32. These are prior-art-search priorities, not findings of patentability.

A true invention audit still requires claim construction, dated conception/reduction-to-practice evidence, patent/non-patent literature searching, inventor contribution analysis, enablement review and jurisdiction-specific legal analysis.

what the Aug. 6+ site list changes

URLs supplied2,153
HTML1,340

Deduplication rule: a public URL is not automatically a project and a project is not automatically an invention. Mirror forms such as project.html and project/index.html, version branches, documentation subfolders, generated datasets, and repeated READMEs are collapsed before counting. The supplied list is treated as the authoritative publication inventory; the Aug. 31 archive snapshot remains the deeper content source for the original 761-family score.

52 provisional documentation-only candidates

These are source-backed project families with an independently describable mechanism or architecture that were not represented as standalone scored HTML families. They are provisional: source-authored claims such as “patent pending,” “trademarked,” or “world’s first” are preserved as source text but are not accepted as audit findings.

what stayed out of the count

Explicit placeholders, category indexes, generic repository shells, duplicated innovations/ and regenerative-innovations/ copies, documentation subfolders for a single parent project, and highly speculative or safety-sensitive concepts lacking enough evidence were retained as watchlist material rather than promoted into the 258 headline set.

03 · methodology

what was actually measured

28% distinctiveness proxy

Rarity of the project’s concept mix across the archive plus title specificity. This detects internal differentiation, not worldwide novelty.

22% implementation

Archive maturity signal plus status weighting. Interactive prototypes and field-test candidates score above unimplemented speculation.

15% evidence

Uses the archive’s evidence signal: sources, methods, uncertainty, corroboration and validation language. It is not an appraisal of source quality.

10% safety

Rewards visible safeguards, consent, privacy, reversibility, auditability, uncertainty and zero-harm framing.

10% reproducibility

Uses structured features and distinct builds as a proxy for whether another person can inspect, copy, export or reproduce the mechanism.

15% independence

Penalizes families with many aliases/versions so iterative copies do not masquerade as separate inventions.

Threshold: audit score ≥58 enters the headline innovation-candidate count. The threshold was chosen before reviewing individual names in the final table and yields 206 candidates. Adjusting the threshold changes the count; the file exposes every record so reviewers can challenge it.
archive-native status definitions used by the audit
{
  "established idea": "Uses practices with an existing real-world evidence base; this archive instance is still not independently validated.",
  "integration": "Combines known ideas or components in a distinctive architecture; integration value is plausible, not proven.",
  "hypothesis": "Makes a testable proposition that requires evidence, falsification criteria, and independent review.",
  "experimental prototype": "An interactive or technical demonstration suitable for controlled evaluation, not operational reliance.",
  "field-test candidate": "Structured enough for an ethics-reviewed, bounded, reversible pilot with monitoring and stop conditions.",
  "speculative concept": "Exploratory future-facing idea; mechanism, feasibility, or impact is substantially unverified."
}

04 · high-priority architecture review

what deserves human scrutiny first

architecture candidate

genesis foundry / root control plane

Routes users through a modular ecosystem, tracks maturity and state, and preserves local-first sovereignty rather than collapsing all functions into one app.

prior-art-heavy integration candidate

occupation_atlas multidimensional model

Distinctive value is the combined task/capability/reward/risk/impact/pathway object model; occupation/task atlases themselves are established.

rename + prior-art review

reward_dna environment vectors

The environmental rather than psychotyping orientation is worth investigating, but “Rewards DNA” is already in commercial use.

high-priority method candidate

progen_engine successor-role synthesis

Uses current occupations, transferable capabilities, reward preservation and unmet system needs to synthesize successor roles.

integration/system candidate

regenerative_careers workforce OS

Combines pathways, bridge plans, curricula, portfolios, evidence, credentials, simulations, on-ramps, enterprise routes and outcomes.

specific interoperability candidate

genesis knowledge-pack exchange

Generic knowledge packs have prior art; the auditable module envelope, merge-by-id and cross-domain schema semantics are the more defensible claim surface.

research-framework candidate

world-building narrative equations

Treats narrative as a model layer connecting evidence, domains, values, scenarios and governance while explicitly separating fiction from evidence.

applied method candidate

edible-canopy safety-gated planning

Combines site scoring, soil/road exposure gates, stewardship requirements, guild selection, action generation and printable field sheets.

applied epistemic method candidate

cognitive-safety incident ledger

Prioritizes observable artifacts, alternative explanations, corroboration and reproducibility over accusation or pattern intensity.

systems-integration candidate

planetary restoration OS

Organizes restoration as a modular operating architecture linking diagnosis, interventions, deployment, evidence and feedback across places.

05 · external spot checks

where broad novelty claims already weaken

These are current web spot checks, not an exhaustive patent search. They are included because an audit should actively search for disconfirming evidence.

high prior-art risk

reward_dna naming / incentive systems

Naming collision and substantial adjacent prior art. A current Rewards DNA service publishes total-rewards, incentive, job-architecture and decision-system material. Treat the name and broad incentive-system concept as prior-art-heavy; any claim should focus on the archive’s specific environment-vector and successor-reward mechanisms.

source ↗

high prior-art risk

occupation / task atlas

Occupation-to-task and transferable-skill atlases exist publicly. ARK’s Atlas maps 1,016 occupations and 18,797 tasks against transferable skills and AI exposure. Novelty claims should therefore focus on the archive’s combined task + capability + reward + risk + impact + successor pathway structure, not on “occupation atlas” alone.

source ↗

high prior-art risk

regenerative careers

Regenerative job and workforce programs exist. REAP Climate Center describes a Regenerative Jobs Program connecting training pathways to community and industry needs. Claim integration architecture, local-first evidence portfolios, successor-role synthesis or demand-creation mechanisms rather than the broad idea of regenerative careers.

source ↗

high prior-art risk

knowledge packs / interoperability

“Knowledge pack” is an established 2026 term across multiple AI tooling projects. Portable, versioned knowledge bundles with provenance already exist. The stronger candidate is the particular Genesis envelope plus merge semantics and cross-module occupation/skill/reward interoperability—not the generic phrase.

source ↗

medium prior-art risk

ai collective governance

External 2026 examples explicitly describe AI collective participation with preserved human authority. Chronology may still matter for precedence analysis, but novelty cannot be inferred from phrase similarity alone.

source ↗

07 · review workflow

turn the estimate into a defensible ledger

1 · chronology

Locate earliest private conception, first implementation, first public publication and every material revision.

2 · claim unit

Write the smallest mechanism actually being claimed. Avoid claiming an entire platform when novelty lives in one narrow subsystem.

3 · prior art

Search patents, papers, standards, products, repositories and institutional practice. Record the closest analog and the surviving difference.

4 · enablement

Ask whether a skilled person could reproduce the mechanism from the materials. Separate working code from aspirational language.

5 · validation

Specify falsifiers, safety boundaries, pilot conditions, outcome measures and stop conditions.

6 · verdict

Classify as known pattern, distinctive integration, research hypothesis, invention candidate, validated method, or abandoned claim.

Click any row in the ledger to open the review drawer. Your manual verdict, prior-art status and notes are stored locally in IndexedDB with localStorage fallback, and can be exported as JSON.

limitations

This audit is corpus-derived. Internal distinctiveness is not legal novelty. Evidence score is documentation signal, not truth. Maturity is artifact completeness, not deployment readiness.
